name: Hiddai
overview: Hiddai is a male figure identified in Scripture as one of David's elite warriors, specifically noted as the nineteenth member of "the thirty." He is uniquely described as being "of the brooks of Gaash," which situates him geographically but does not specify his tribal affiliation. Beyond this, there are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Hiddai appears in 2 Samuel 23:30 without an explicit meaning provided, indicating it is a proper name used without special divine attribution. Another name, Hurai, is associated with the same individual in 1 Chronicles 11:32, but similarly lacks a given meaning or title, suggesting these are simply personal names recorded in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Hiddai beyond his identification with the brooks of Gaash and his role among David's warriors. There are no listed relatives or connections to other biblical figures in the provided data.
scriptureSignificance: Hiddai's significance lies primarily in his inclusion among David's elite fighters, known as "the thirty," highlighting his role in the military strength that supported David's reign. His mention underscores the diversity and regional representation within David's forces, with Hiddai coming from a specific locale, the brooks of Gaash. Although details about his personal life are sparse, his place in the biblical narrative reflects the faithful service of David's men during a foundational period in Israel's history.
